strengths: Addresses an important efficiency problem in multimodal computer vision. Reducing visual tokens before the language model is a practical design that can complement backbone compression and quantization.

Evaluation covers six image benchmarks, two language-model sizes, and three video benchmarks. PruMerge+ reports a useful tradeoff at 25% token retention: for example, 7B TextVQA scores 57.1 versus 58.2, while MMBench scores 64.9 versus 64.3.
Transfer to Video-LLaVA without additional training is promising. PruMerge substantially reduces the reported token count while improving ActivityNet-QA accuracy from 45.3 to 48.3.

Tables 4–6 provide useful component analyses: the method outperforms the tested spatial-sampling baselines, token supplementation improves the compressed model, and fine-tuning recovers additional performance.

The high-level pipeline is understandable, and foundational models, training methods, and relevant token-reduction work are cited. The appendix appropriately acknowledges lossy compression, limited validation, and potential misuse.
weaknesses: The performance-preservation claims exceed the evidence. In Table 1, even after fine-tuning, 7B PruMerge reduces VQAv2 from 78.5 to 72.0, POPE from 85.9 to 76.3, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3. These are meaningful losses. Section 4.1 also incorrectly claims improved POPE performance. Compression can justify reduced accuracy, but the scientific case should establish a favorable tradeoff rather than repeatedly describe performance as uncompromised.

The comparisons do not adequately establish the contribution beyond existing pruning and merging ideas. Table 4 tests first-token selection and uniform grids, without comparing against attention-based fixed top-k selection or an adapted ToMe baseline at matched token budgets and training conditions. The ablations do not isolate the benefit of adaptive IQR allocation, and PruMerge+ gains are confounded with its larger token budget.

Practical efficiency remains insufficiently validated. Table 2 provides roofline estimates for language-model prefill. Measured end-to-end latency and peak memory, including visual encoding and pruning/merging overhead, are absent. Decoding, variable-length batching, and PruMerge+ efficiency are also unreported, leaving the deployment benefits and the strongest accuracy-efficiency operating point unverified.

Important implementation details are missing or inconsistent. Algorithm 1 leaves the neighbor count k and attention-head aggregation unspecified. As written, its update excludes the selected center and forms an unnormalized weighted sum of neighboring tokens, whereas the surrounding description discusses supplementing selected tokens through weighted averaging. Cluster-overlap handling and LoRA configuration are also insufficiently specified for reproduction.

PruMerge+'s reported token budget cannot be reconciled with Algorithm 1. The algorithm adds m uniformly sampled tokens to m outliers, which would imply approximately 11% retention when PruMerge retains 5.5%, rather than Table 1's 25%. Its loop and output also remain indexed over only m tokens. This affects reproduction of a principal result and requires an explicit, corrected algorithm and per-benchmark token counts.
